source: Carlos 2026-09-20: try a quiet Milky Way snow night with warm fortress windows. Local implementation following the pasted design advice; no downloaded shader package.
direction_note: Azimuth is measured from world -Z towards +X. Camera-relative yaw is resolved once at configure(), then stays anchored in world space. Elevation is above the world horizon. Tilt 0 follows the local sky horizon; positive values climb toward camera-right.
lighting_note: Sky cubemap renders only the blue gradient. Independent ambient color / moonlight must be configured in the Panti look; raising Milky Way brightness is not used to light snow.
motion_note: Shared explicit anim_t drives slow spatially offset star twinkle; no TIME. During the 8-second period transition, the caller rotates the real sky in world azimuth and redraws the star viewport; after easing to midnight it renders once and holds. Shared pause freezes both motion and rendering.
render_note: The original opaque scene and its DOF remain intact; its native Sky draws base color and Milky Way dust. A second viewport shares the same World3D and matching camera/DOF but has a white background, yielding a soft sky mask from its color difference. One empty-world viewport (static at endpoints, re-rendered during sky flow) renders sharp stars only. A CanvasLayer adds those stars through the difference mask. No geometry is duplicated and there are no depth writes or transparent scene backgrounds.
twinkle_revision: Carlos: keep the stronger star twinkle after reaching stable midnight; the eight-second period transition remains one step stronger.
